sections.title: The roster table
sections.intro: A global in init.lua and its modules, and also require("roster"). A Plugin gets a bigger one: the Plugin API.

entries.heading: roster.os
entries.about: The OS the app runs on. Read-only.

entries.heading: roster.api_version
entries.about: The version of this table, raised when it changes. Read-only. The Plugin API's version too: it rises with that.
entries.example: if roster.api_version >= 4 then roster.o.vim = false end

entries.heading: roster.version
entries.about: The app's version. Read-only.
entries.example: if roster.version:match("^0%.2") then roster.o.auto_reload = true end

entries.heading: roster.config_dir
entries.about: The config folder: where init.lua is, as this machine writes the path. Read-only. For messages and comparisons; require already looks there.

entries.heading: roster.o
entries.about: Every option, as a table you assign to and read: roster.o.terminal.size = "16pt". Nested objects need no setup. An unknown name is an error at its line, with the name meant; a value of the wrong type too. Reading an option gives the value set so far (a copy), or nil; reading an object, a map or a list gives its table, with the methods its kind has (roster.o.Object, roster.o.Map, roster.o.List). Assigning a whole table replaces that branch; assigning one roster.o table to another option copies what it holds (what init.lua set, else its default), and one that holds neither is an error. The table init.lua returns, if any, wins over what roster.o sets.
entries.example:
roster.o.terminal.size = "16pt"
roster.o.terminal.font:prepend("Cascadia Mono")
if roster.o.vim then roster.o.keys.leader.p = "connect esx-02" end

entries.heading: roster.o.get(name)
entries.about: Reads any option by its dotted name: a copy of what init.lua set there, or nil. The read that always works: a map's key named like a method (get, has, keys, reset) reads as that key here, set or not. A table comes back as a plain copy, to walk with pairs(). An unknown name is an error at its line.

rows.name: name
rows.about: An option's dotted name: "terminal.size", "views.get".

entries.example:
local views = roster.o.get("views") or {}
for id in pairs(views) do print(id) end

entries.heading: roster.o.reset(name)
entries.about: Puts an option back to its default: what init.lua set there is taken away. Any option: a value, an object, a map or a list. An unknown name is an error at its line.

rows.name: name
rows.about: An option's dotted name: "terminal.size".

entries.heading: roster.set(name, value)
entries.about: Sets any option by its dotted name, as roster.o does. The same store as roster.o: the last write wins. The name and the value are checked at the call's line. The returned table wins over a call that sets the same option.

rows.name: name
rows.about: An option's dotted name: "terminal.size".

rows.name: value
rows.about: Its value, as the option takes it; nil resets it.

entries.heading: roster.keymap.set(context, keys, action)
entries.about: Binds a key, as keys.<context> does. A later set of the same keys replaces it. An unknown context is an error at its line.

rows.name: context
rows.about: The keymap's context.

rows.name: keys
rows.about: A chord or a sequence of chords separated by spaces: "Ctrl+n", "d d".

rows.name: action
rows.about: A command line, or false to unbind a default.

entries.heading: roster.keymap.del(context, keys)
entries.about: Takes off a key binding init.lua made. Keys init.lua didn't bind are an error at the line; to unbind one of roster's own, set it to false.

rows.name: context
rows.about: The keymap's context.

rows.name: keys
rows.about: The keys, as set took them.

entries.heading: roster.keymap.get(context, keys)
entries.about: The action init.lua bound to keys, or nil. Roster's own bindings aren't in it.

rows.name: context
rows.about: The keymap's context.

rows.name: keys
rows.about: The keys, as set took them.

entries.example: if not roster.keymap.get("leader", "p") then roster.keymap.set("leader", "p", "close") end

entries.heading: roster.keymap.list(context)
entries.about: A copy of init.lua's bindings in a context: keys → action. An empty table when it binds none there.

rows.name: context
rows.about: The keymap's context.

entries.example: for keys, action in pairs(roster.keymap.list("leader")) do print(keys, action) end

entries.heading: roster.themes.define(id, theme)
entries.about: Defines a Theme, as themes.<id> does. An id already defined is an error naming both lines (change it with update); a bundled Theme's id too.

rows.name: id
rows.about: The Theme's id: not "auto", not a bundled Theme's.

rows.name: theme
rows.about: A Theme spec.

entries.heading: roster.themes.update(id, fields)
entries.about: Changes a Theme: one init.lua defined, or a bundled one (which becomes a changed copy of itself). An id that is neither is an error at its line.

rows.name: id
rows.about: A Theme init.lua defined, or a bundled one.

rows.name: fields
rows.about: What to change: tables (colors, terminal, ansi) merge token by token.

entries.heading: roster.themes.remove(id)
entries.about: Removes a Theme init.lua defined (or its changes to a bundled one). A bundled Theme init.lua didn't change, or an id it doesn't have, is an error at its line.

rows.name: id
rows.about: A Theme init.lua defined.

entries.heading: roster.themes.get(id)
entries.about: A copy of init.lua's spec for a Theme, or nil. Nil for a bundled Theme init.lua didn't change.

rows.name: id
rows.about: A Theme's id.

entries.example:
local paper = roster.themes.get("paper")
if paper then print(paper.label) end

entries.heading: roster.themes.list()
entries.about: Every Theme's id: the bundled ones, then init.lua's.
entries.example: for _, id in ipairs(roster.themes.list()) do print(id) end

entries.heading: roster.packages.add(...)
entries.about: Adds Packages, from any file of the Config. Two Packages with the same name are an error naming both lines. Fetching is a command: :packages update.

rows.about: Package specs: { SOURCE, tag = … } or just SOURCE.

entries.heading: roster.packages.remove(name)
entries.about: Takes a Package out of the Config. A name it doesn't have is an error at its line. Its folder stays until :packages clean.

rows.name: name
rows.about: Its name (letter case aside).

entries.heading: roster.packages.update(name, fields)
entries.about: Changes a Package's spec: pin a tag, change its config. A name it doesn't have, or a field a Package spec doesn't have, is an error at its line.

rows.name: name
rows.about: Its name (letter case aside).

rows.name: fields
rows.about: Fields to set over the spec's; a tag, branch or commit replaces the other two.

entries.heading: roster.packages.get(name)
entries.about: A copy of a Package's spec, or nil. Its source is in source.

rows.name: name
rows.about: Its name (letter case aside).

entries.example:
local alerts = roster.packages.get("recent-alerts")
if alerts then print(alerts.tag) end

entries.heading: roster.packages.list()
entries.about: Copies of every Package's spec, in order.
entries.example: for _, p in ipairs(roster.packages.list()) do print(p.source) end

entries.heading: roster.packages.has(name)
entries.about: Whether the Config has a Package by that name.

rows.name: name
rows.about: Its name (letter case aside).

entries.example: if not roster.packages.has("pinned") then roster.packages.add("someone/pinned") end

entries.heading: roster.folders.add(...)
entries.about: Adds Folders, from any file of the Config. Two Folders with the same name (letter case aside) are an error naming both lines.

rows.about: Folder specs: { name = …, hosts = { … } }.

entries.heading: roster.folders.remove(name)
entries.about: Takes a Folder out of the Config. A name it doesn't have is an error at its line.

rows.name: name
rows.about: Its name (letter case aside).

entries.heading: roster.folders.update(name, fields)
entries.about: Changes a Folder: rename it, or give it other Hosts. A name it doesn't have is an error at its line; a new name another Folder has names both lines.

rows.name: name
rows.about: Its name (letter case aside).

rows.name: fields
rows.about: Fields to set over the Folder's: name, hosts.

entries.heading: roster.folders.get(name)
entries.about: A copy of a Folder's spec, or nil.

rows.name: name
rows.about: Its name (letter case aside).

entries.example:
local lab = roster.folders.get("Lab")
if lab then print(#lab.hosts) end

entries.heading: roster.folders.list()
entries.about: Copies of every Folder's spec, in order.
entries.example: for _, f in ipairs(roster.folders.list()) do print(f.name) end

entries.heading: roster.folders.has(name)
entries.about: Whether the Config has a Folder by that name.

rows.name: name
rows.about: Its name (letter case aside).

entries.heading: roster.folders.add_hosts(name, hosts)
entries.about: Adds Hosts to the end of a Folder. A Host it has already, or a Folder it doesn't have, is an error at its line.

rows.name: name
rows.about: Its name (letter case aside).

rows.name: hosts
rows.about: A Host's name, or a list of them.

entries.heading: roster.folders.remove_hosts(name, hosts)
entries.about: Takes Hosts out of a Folder. A Host it doesn't have, or a Folder it doesn't have, is an error at its line.

rows.name: name
rows.about: Its name (letter case aside).

rows.name: hosts
rows.about: A Host's name, or a list of them.

sections.title: The tables of roster.o
sections.intro: Reading an object, a map or a list from roster.o gives its table, with these methods (call them with a colon: roster.o.terminal.font:append("Hack")). Each option's entry lists what its kind takes; a value is read and assigned as it is.

entries.heading: roster.o.Object:get()
entries.about: A copy of what init.lua set in an object (a table of named options), or nil. Defaults aren't in it: only what was set.
entries.example:
local t = roster.o.terminal:get()
if t then print(t.size) end

entries.heading: roster.o.Object:reset()
entries.about: Puts every option in an object back to its default.

entries.heading: roster.o.Map:get()
entries.about: A copy of a map (a table keyed by names you pick): key → value, or nil when nothing is set. Read one key with map.KEY; set one with map.KEY = value, remove it with map.KEY = nil.
entries.example:
local views = roster.o.views:get() or {}
for id in pairs(views) do print(id) end

entries.heading: roster.o.Map:has(key)
entries.about: Whether init.lua set this key of a map. A key named like a method (get, has, keys, reset) reads as that key once init.lua has set it, and as the method until then; roster.o.get(name) always reads and roster.o.reset(name) always resets.

rows.name: key
rows.about: A key.

entries.example: if not roster.o.views:has("topology") then roster.o.views.topology = { place = "panel" } end

entries.heading: roster.o.Map:keys()
entries.about: The keys init.lua set in a map.
entries.example: for _, id in ipairs(roster.o.themes:keys()) do print(id) end

entries.heading: roster.o.Map:reset()
entries.about: Takes away every key init.lua set in a map: it's back to its default.

entries.heading: roster.o.List:get()
entries.about: A copy of a list, or nil when init.lua didn't set it.
entries.example:
local fonts = roster.o.terminal.font:get()
if fonts then print(#fonts) end

entries.heading: roster.o.List:append(...)
entries.about: Adds items to the end of a list. An unset list starts from its default. A list that takes each item once refuses one it has, at the line.

rows.about: Items to add.

entries.heading: roster.o.List:prepend(...)
entries.about: Adds items to the start of a list, in the order given. As append.

rows.about: Items to add.

entries.heading: roster.o.List:insert(i, value)
entries.about: Puts an item at a position of a list. A position outside the list is an error at the line.

rows.name: i
rows.about: The position, from 1 to the list's length + 1.

rows.name: value
rows.about: The item.

entries.heading: roster.o.List:remove(...)
entries.about: Takes items out of a list. An item it doesn't have is an error at the line.

rows.about: Items to take out (for folders and packages, a name will do).

entries.heading: roster.o.List:has(value)
entries.about: Whether a list has an item, its default counted while it's unset.

rows.name: value
rows.about: An item (for folders and packages, a name will do).

entries.example: if not roster.o.terminal.font:has("Hack") then roster.o.terminal.font:append("Hack") end

entries.heading: roster.o.List:clear()
entries.about: Empties a list.

entries.heading: roster.o.List:reset()
entries.about: Puts a list back to its default.

entries.heading: theme
entries.about: The Theme to use, or "auto" to follow the OS's light or dark setting with dark_theme and light_theme.
entries.takes: a Theme's id, or "auto"

entries.heading: dark_theme
entries.about: The Theme "auto" picks while the OS is dark.
entries.takes: a Theme's id

entries.heading: light_theme
entries.about: The Theme "auto" picks while the OS is light.
entries.takes: a Theme's id

entries.heading: themes
entries.about: New Themes, or changed copies of bundled ones, by id: each a Theme spec.

entries.heading: colors
entries.about: UI colour tokens set over whichever Theme is in use.

entries.heading: fonts
entries.about: The UI's fonts.

entries.heading: fonts.ui
entries.about: The UI's font.
entries.takes: a family name, or a CSS font stack (anything with a comma)

entries.heading: fonts.mono
entries.about: The wordmark's and code-like UI text's font.
entries.takes: a family name, or a CSS font stack

entries.heading: fonts.ui_size
entries.about: The UI's text size; the smaller steps, the row height and the Sidebar's width follow it.
entries.takes: 11 to 20 px

entries.heading: ui
entries.about: The rest of the UI's look.

entries.heading: ui.hints
entries.about: false hides every keycap hint. Unset, :hints decides and the State keeps its choice; set, it wins.

entries.heading: ui.messages
entries.about: What the message line shows: errors, warnings and answers only ("quiet"), or routine confirmations too ("all"). Unset, :messages decides.

entries.heading: terminal
entries.about: The terminal's font, look and behaviour.

entries.heading: terminal.font
entries.about: Font families, most wanted first: the first one installed is used.
entries.takes: a font name, a CSS font stack, or a list of names; each item once

entries.heading: terminal.size
entries.about: The font size: a number is px, "16pt" is points (as Windows Terminal converts them), "21px" works too.
entries.takes: 6 to 72 px (4.5 to 54 pt)

entries.heading: terminal.weight
entries.about: The font weight; the bundled Iosevka has 400, 500 and 700.

entries.heading: terminal.bold_weight
entries.about: The weight of bold (SGR 1) text.

entries.heading: terminal.bold_is_bright
entries.about: Bold text in the bright ANSI colours too.

entries.heading: terminal.line_height
entries.about: A multiple of the font's own line height.

entries.heading: terminal.cell_height
entries.about: A multiple of the font size, as Windows Terminal's cellHeight; wins over line_height.

entries.heading: terminal.renderer
entries.about: WebGL (fast) or the DOM (the browser's own text rendering).

entries.heading: terminal.cursor_style
entries.about: The cursor's shape.

entries.heading: terminal.scrollback
entries.about: How many lines the terminal keeps above the screen.
entries.takes: 0 to 1000000 lines

entries.heading: terminal.copy_on_select
entries.about: Selecting text copies it.

entries.heading: terminal.right_click_paste
entries.about: Right-click copies the selection, or pastes when there's none.

entries.heading: terminal.colors
entries.about: Any terminal or ANSI colour, set over the Theme's.

entries.heading: terminal.shell_hooks
entries.about: Send each Session's shell the line that turns on prompt marks (OSC 133) and its folder (OSC 7). Unset, a Host's shell_hooks in roster.yml decides.

entries.heading: leader
entries.about: The chord that takes the keyboard back from a terminal.
entries.takes: a chord: "Ctrl+Space", "ctrl+b", "C-b" or "<C-b>", with Ctrl, Alt or Meta

entries.heading: vim
entries.about: j/k/h/l/gg/G in lists and the Picker.

entries.heading: keys
entries.about: Key bindings, per context: key or sequence → action.

entries.heading: keys.leader
entries.about: After the Leader: key or sequence (chords separated by spaces: "d d") → key action.

entries.heading: keys.list
entries.about: In a list (the Sidebar): key or sequence (chords separated by spaces: "d d") → key action.

entries.heading: keys.list_vim
entries.about: In a list while vim keys are on: key or sequence (chords separated by spaces: "d d") → key action.

entries.heading: keys.picker
entries.about: In the Picker and every finder: key or sequence (chords separated by spaces: "d d") → key action.

entries.heading: keys.picker_vim
entries.about: In the Picker's list while vim keys are on: key or sequence (chords separated by spaces: "d d") → key action.

entries.heading: keys.cmdline
entries.about: In the : command line: key or sequence (chords separated by spaces: "d d") → key action.

entries.heading: keys.terminal
entries.about: In a terminal, before the shell sees the key: key or sequence (chords separated by spaces: "d d") → key action.

entries.heading: keys.global
entries.about: Everywhere, with no Leader (keep it to keys a shell doesn't use): key or sequence (chords separated by spaces: "d d") → key action.

entries.heading: default_mode
entries.about: The view mode at start (read at start only).

entries.heading: sessions
entries.about: Open Sessions in the Sidebar, or in a tab strip.

entries.heading: modes
entries.about: Each view mode's layout.

entries.heading: modes.standard
entries.about: The Standard mode's pieces; a piece left out keeps this mode's default.

entries.heading: modes.standard.titlebar
entries.about: The title bar.

entries.heading: modes.standard.sidebar

entries.takes: true, false, or a table of the options below (which shows it)

entries.heading: modes.standard.sidebar.side
entries.about: The side of the window it's on.

entries.heading: modes.standard.sidebar.sections

entries.takes: section ids in order: "sessions", "folders", "inventory", or a Plugin section's id; each item once

entries.heading: modes.standard.sessionbar
entries.about: The thin tmux-style bar of open Sessions, and its edge.

entries.heading: modes.standard.statusbar
entries.about: The status bar, and its segments.
entries.takes: true, false, or segments in order: "backend", "box", "hosts", "path", "changes", "hints", "mode"; each item once

entries.heading: modes.standard.fullscreen
entries.about: OS fullscreen.

entries.heading: modes.standard.toolbar
entries.about: The controls for common commands, in the title bar (or a bar of their own without one).
entries.takes: true, false, or controls in order: "sidebar", "find", "quick", "add", "changes", "publish", "details", "cmdline", "keys", "help", "lock", "mode", or a Plugin control's id; each item once

entries.heading: modes.focus
entries.about: The Focus mode's pieces; a piece left out keeps this mode's default.

entries.heading: modes.focus.titlebar
entries.about: The title bar.

entries.heading: modes.focus.sidebar
entries.about: The Sidebar: shown or hidden, the side it's on, and its sections.
entries.takes: true, false, or a table of the options below (which shows it)

entries.heading: modes.focus.sidebar.side
entries.about: The side of the window it's on.

entries.heading: modes.focus.sidebar.sections
entries.about: Its sections, in order; all of them when left out.
entries.takes: section ids in order: "sessions", "folders", "inventory", or a Plugin section's id; each item once

entries.heading: modes.focus.sessionbar
entries.about: The thin tmux-style bar of open Sessions, and its edge.

entries.heading: modes.focus.statusbar
entries.about: The status bar, and its segments.
entries.takes: true, false, or segments in order: "backend", "box", "hosts", "path", "changes", "hints", "mode"; each item once

entries.heading: modes.focus.fullscreen
entries.about: OS fullscreen.

entries.heading: modes.focus.toolbar
entries.about: The controls for common commands, in the title bar (or a bar of their own without one).
entries.takes: true, false, or controls in order: "sidebar", "find", "quick", "add", "changes", "publish", "details", "cmdline", "keys", "help", "lock", "mode", or a Plugin control's id; each item once

entries.heading: panel
entries.about: What every panel and view starts with.

entries.heading: panel.width
entries.about: A docked panel's width, for every panel and view views doesn't give one. Unset, each keeps its own.
entries.takes: 10 to 95 percent of the window

entries.heading: views
entries.about: Per panel or view id (help, details, a Plugin view's id): where it opens first, and its width.

entries.heading: folders
entries.about: Folders kept in the Config, read-only in the app: each a Folder spec.

entries.heading: vault
entries.about: This Box's own vault settings, over roster.yml's providers. Paths and choices, never a secret.
entries.example: roster.o.vault = { save_to = { organization = "My Team", collection = "Infra logins" } }

entries.heading: vault.save_to
entries.ty: "personal"|{ organization: string, collection: string }|{ group: string }
entries.about: Where Save to vault puts a new password by default.
entries.takes: "personal", { organization = …, collection = … } (Bitwarden) or { group = … } (KeePassXC)

entries.heading: vault.kp
entries.about: KeePassXC's files, on the Box roster runs on.

entries.heading: vault.kp.database
entries.about: KeePassXC's .kdbx.
entries.takes: an absolute path, or one starting with ~

entries.heading: vault.kp.key_file

entries.takes: an absolute path, or one starting with ~

entries.heading: packages
entries.about: Plugins fetched from git repos and pinned in roster.lock: each a Package spec, or just its source.

entries.heading: plugin_proxy
entries.about: The proxy Plugins' requests to public names go through. Unset, they go direct.
entries.takes: http://HOST:PORT, the port written out, with no user or password

entries.heading: idle_lock_minutes
entries.about: Lock after this many minutes without input.
entries.takes: 1 to 1440 minutes

entries.heading: pull_fresh_minutes

entries.heading: auto_reload

entries.heading: editor

entries.heading: backend
entries.about: Which roster the app runs: detected, this machine's, or WSL's.
entries.takes: "auto", "local", "wsl" or "wsl:<distro>"

entries.heading: roster_command
entries.about: The command that runs roster, for development: a command line (split on spaces) or a list of words. Unset, roster.
entries.takes: roster itself: "roster", a path ending in /roster, or "uv run --project <dir> roster"

sections.title: Types
sections.intro: The tables some options hold, by the names :config types gives them.

entries.heading: roster.config.Theme
entries.about: A Theme spec: a bundled Theme (base) with tokens changed, or a new one.

rows.name: label
rows.about: Its name in the app; the id when left out.

rows.name: appearance
rows.about: Which OS appearance it suits; the base's when left out.

rows.name: base
rows.about: The Theme it starts from: every token it doesn't set comes from there (Roster dark, or Roster light for appearance = "light", when left out). Takes a Theme's id.

rows.name: colors
rows.about: UI colour tokens over the base's.

rows.name: terminal
rows.about: The terminal's colours, apart from the 16 ANSI ones, over the base's.

rows.name: ansi
rows.about: The 16 ANSI colours; false keeps the standard palette even when the base has its own; the base's when left out.

entries.heading: roster.config.KeyAction
entries.about: A key action: the command line a key runs, or false to unbind a default.
entries.takes: a command line, exactly what you'd type after : ("close", "session 1"), or false

entries.heading: roster.config.View
entries.about: A view spec: one panel's or view's default place and width.

rows.name: place
rows.about: Docked beside the terminal, or over the whole window.

rows.name: width
rows.about: Its docked width. Takes 10 to 95 percent of the window.

entries.heading: roster.config.Folder
entries.about: A Folder spec: a name and the Hosts in it.

rows.name: name
rows.about: The Folder's name. Takes unique, ignoring case, with no double quote.

rows.name: hosts
rows.about: The Hosts in it, in order. Takes Host names; each item once.

entries.heading: roster.config.Package
entries.about: A Package spec: { SOURCE, tag = …, config = { … } }, or just SOURCE.

rows.name: source
rows.about: Where the repo is: the spec's first item, or source = …. Takes "owner/repo" (GitHub), or a git URL: https://…, ssh://…, git@host:path, file://… or a full path.

rows.name: name
rows.about: Its name (its folder and its line in roster.lock); the repo's (or dir's) name when left out.

rows.name: tag
rows.about: The tag to pin. At most one of tag, branch and commit; none means the default branch.

rows.name: branch
rows.about: The branch to follow.

rows.name: commit
rows.about: The commit to pin. Takes 4 to 40 hex digits.

rows.name: dir
rows.about: The repo's folder that holds the Plugin, when it isn't the top. Takes a folder inside the repo, relative, / between folders, no ...

rows.name: config
rows.about: Settings the Package reads as roster.plugin.config. Takes a table (never a function).
